items.definition:
A person who breaks into a building illegally, typically with the intent to steal.
The police caught the burglar trying to escape through the window.

A two-door car with a fixed roof and a sloping rear.
He drove a sleek sports coupe.

A small fragment of bread, cake, or biscuit.
The bird pecked at the bread crumbs on the ground.

festival; party
The town held a lively fiesta to celebrate its patron saint.

a man from France
He met a friendly Frenchman on his trip to Paris.

a movable joint on which a door, gate, or lid swings
The door creaked loudly on its rusty hinge.

a device for holding a door or gate closed
Make sure the garden gate has a secure latch.

an apparatus for making fabric by weaving yarn or thread
The weaver worked tirelessly at her loom.

corn
Farmers grow maize in large fields.

a compilation of songs recorded in a specific order
He made a mixtape of his favorite songs for her.

a sitting room in a private house
We gathered in the parlor for tea.

a small smooth rounded stone
I picked up a smooth pebble from the beach.

a person who is qualified to prepare and dispense medicinal drugs
The pharmacist advised me on how to take the new medication.

a device for heating a room or vehicle
The radiator in the living room keeps the house warm.

a game or round immediately preceding the final
Our team won the semifinal and advanced to the championship.

an outline of subjects in a course of study
The professor handed out the course syllabus on the first day.

the northern part of a state
They live upstate, away from the city.

a strip of porous material in a candle or lamp
The candle's wick was too short.

the feeling of being annoyed; something that annoys
The constant noise was a great annoyance.

A large outdoor fire.
We gathered around the bonfire and told stories.

A person who leads cheers at sporting events.
She joined the cheerleading squad in high school.

The panel in a car containing controls and instruments.
The warning light on the dashboard came on.

A short journey or trip.
We went on an excursion to the mountains.

a soft candy made from sugar, butter, and milk or cream
My grandmother makes the best chocolate fudge.

a printed sheet of paper, often folded, containing information or advertising
The tourist office provides free leaflets about local attractions.

a permit from an authority to own or use something (UK spelling)
You need a driving licence to operate a car.

a limousine (informal)
They arrived at the event in a stretch limo.

The long hair on the neck of a horse or lion.
The lion shook its magnificent mane.

A cosmetic for darkening and thickening eyelashes.
She applied mascara to her eyelashes before going out.

A type of glove, especially one used in baseball.
The baseball player caught the ball in his mitt.

A pattern of crisscrossed horizontal and vertical bands in multiple colors.
He wore a shirt with a red and black plaid pattern.

A loud unpleasant noise; a bat with a long handle and a round or oval frame with an open network of strings, used in tennis, badminton, and squash.
The children were making a terrible racket upstairs.

a circular intersection
Take the third exit at the roundabout.

the act of putting your signature on something; a new player or employee
The signing of the peace treaty took place yesterday.

a tool for digging; a suit of playing cards
He used a spade to dig a hole for the new plant.

a greenish-blue color; a precious stone of this color
She wore a beautiful turquoise necklace.

the quality of being useful
The usefulness of the new tool was immediately apparent.

a mythical person who changes into a wolf
In the story, the man transformed into a werewolf under the full moon.

a person trained to give guidance on personal or psychological problems
She spoke to a school counsellor about her problems.

a painful, involuntary contraction of a muscle or muscles
He got a cramp in his leg during the run.

an attractive or endearing person or animal
Her little brother is such a cutie.

an item of furniture or equipment in a house or room
The apartment came with basic furnishings.

a machine or tool for grinding something
He used a coffee grinder to prepare his beans.

a book bound in stiff covers
I prefer to buy the hardcover edition of books.

a joint of a finger
He cracked his knuckles before starting to type.

a small booklet or leaflet containing information
She picked up a pamphlet about local attractions at the tourist office.

a gnawing mammal of an order that includes rats, mice, squirrels, and beavers
Mice and rats are common types of rodents.

the practice of maintaining the health and appearance of the skin
She has a strict daily skincare routine.

unit of pronunciation
The word 'water' has two syllables.

food to be eaten elsewhere; main point
Let's get a Chinese takeaway tonight.

an electronic system for recording messages
I left a message on his voicemail.

unit of electric potential
The battery provides 12 volts of power.

helicopter (informal); a type of axe
A police chopper was circling overhead.

a line or ridge produced on paper or cloth by folding or pressing
He ironed the crease out of his shirt.

the process of breaking down food
Eating slowly aids digestion.

a mischievous, ugly, dwarf-like creature of folklore
The children dressed up as goblins for Halloween.

a deep purplish-blue color
The sky turned a deep indigo just before sunset.

the central part of a town or city
The new restaurant is located in midtown.

an apartment on the top floor of a tall building
They bought a luxurious penthouse with a view of the city.

an angry argument or disagreement
They had a minor quarrel about who should do the dishes.

a partial refund to someone who has paid too much money for something
Customers can claim a rebate on their energy-efficient appliances.

Japanese cherry blossom
The sakura trees bloom beautifully in spring.

Self-Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus
He learned to use scuba gear for his underwater photography.

the line where a large body of water meets the land
We walked along the shoreline, collecting seashells.
